rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests a multimodal setup with pca_n2000 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. It clarifies whether combining RNA and image data with complex aggregation/fusion strategies improves performance compared to simpler models. This is the best use of the first experiment as it isolates key design choices (multimodal, encoder types, aggregation, fusion) that are critical for the study.

The existing evidence shows that config_002 (multimodal) achieves 0.5856 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether using only RNA data (rna_only) with the same RNA encoder (pca_n2000) and aggregation method (transformer) improves performance, isolating the impact of the image modality. It directly addresses whether multimodal approaches outperform simpler rna_only models, a critical design choice with sparse evidence yet high uncertainty.

Existing evidence shows multimodal models (config_002) outperform RNA-only (config_019). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder (pca_n2000 → scvi_n200) and image encoder (imagenet_vit_l → resnet50) while retaining transformer aggregation and weighted fusion could improve performance. It isolates the impact of encoder choices on multimodal performance, a critical design decision with sparse evidence.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with pca_n2000 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders achieve higher accuracy (0.5856) than rna_only models (0.519). This experiment tests whether changing the aggregation method from transformer (used in config_002) to avgpool affects performance, isolating the impact of this key design choice. It directly addresses uncertainty about aggregation's role while building on the promising multimodal foundation.

Existing evidence shows config_007 (avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.6352). This experiment tests whether changing aggregation to transformer and fusion to concat (config_022) with the same RNA/image encoders could improve performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation/fusion choices, which are critical for multimodal integration, while keeping RNA/image encoders constant. This balances exploration of key design choices with exploitation of the current top-performing setup.

The existing evidence shows that config_007 (avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion, imagenet_vit_l image encoder) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scgpt (while keeping aggregation, fusion, and image encoder unchanged) improves performance. This isolates the impact of RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, and helps determine if scgpt offers better representation than pca_n2000 in this multimodal setup.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l image encoder with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (config_007) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation and concat fusion (while keeping the same image encoder) improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation and fusion choices. It directly compares key design decisions without altering multiple parameters simultaneously.

Existing evidence shows multimodal models (e.g., config_007) outperform rna_only models. However, the RNA encoder (scgpt vs pca_n2000) and its impact on performance remain unclear. Testing config_001 (rna_only with scgpt) isolates the RNA encoder's effect, providing critical insight into whether scgpt's performance in rna_only settings could inform multimodal strategies. This addresses uncertainty about RNA representation choices while balancing exploitation of the current multimodal trend.

Existing evidence shows config_007 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 (config_014) affects performance, isolating the effect of RNA representation. This clarifies if the RNA encoder choice is critical, balancing exploration of key design decisions while building on the top-performing configuration.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_014) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from transformer to avgpool (while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion method the same) affects performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation method, a key design choice, to determine if avgpool could improve or match transformer's effectiveness in this context.
